The topic of data quality within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] reveals significant shortcomings in how patient information and clinical practices are recorded. A primary indicator of this poor data quality is the unusually low number of patients registered from private hospitals, which strongly points to incomplete data collection across the healthcare sector [^src1]. 

Beyond missing patient demographics, the database also suffers from systemic flaws in how clinical work is documented. There are massive problems with current registration practices, resulting in a failure to record various performed elements and treatments [^src1]. Together, these issues compromise the reliability of the database for tracking ADHD care and outcomes, highlighting a critical need for improved data entry protocols.

## Claims

### ADHD_2024.pdf, pages 1-5 (Page 5)
- Der er et meget lavt antal patienter fra privathospitalerne, hvilket tyder på ukomplette data [^src1] (adhd-databasen)
- Der er massive problemer med registreringspraksis, således at udførte elementer ikke registreres [^src1] (adhd-databasen)
